exitCriteria: A new version of studio/contracts/commercial-terms.*.json supersedes v1 and encodes exactly the ratified position: EUR 1,500 standard and EUR 1,000 founding, both inclusive of VAT at the prevailing rate (D-021), foundingCohortSize 25, coupleAccessMonths 18 with the D-022 grace rule represented, and no numeric activation allowance. node scripts/check-venue-edition-contract.mjs has been re-pointed at the ratified figures and exits 0, and its assertions on src/app/layout.tsx publish the two-rate offer rather than one exact price. The gate fails while the enforcement script still asserts the 2026-07-11 position. Evidence: the diff and the passing output. (E02.01, I-002)

Each of E02.01 through E02.12 has a written ratification record naming the position taken, the D-number it derives from, and the position it supersedes, or an explicit statement that there was nothing to supersede. Evidence: a twelve-row table with no empty cell. (E02.01 to E02.12)

The superseded HQ decision is actually superseded in the repository: studio/content/hq/decisions/venue-edition-fixed-price-2026-07-11.md carries a superseded status naming its replacement, and a new dated HQ decision records the Founding 25 position. Evidence: both paths plus node scripts/check-content-truth.mjs passing. I-002 closes with a stated basis, not by lapse. (E02.01, D-009)

A committed string-sweep script, run over a named file list, returns zero hits for the retired commercial position on any surface a venue can reach: no standalone EUR 1,500 without the founding rate, no 'first fifteen', no '40/80', no 'allotment' in venue-facing copy, and zero occurrences of 'for life', 'forever', 'lifetime' or 'guaranteed'. Machine fields scoped out deliberately, never by disabling the sweep when it first trips. Evidence: the script, its output, and the file list. (E02.02, E02.03, E07.07, R-008, R-020)

The published price-reduction wording is the single ratified sentence from D-009 point 2 and nothing else. The sweep confirms 'one-third', '33.3%' and '33%' appear on no venue-facing surface. Evidence: the sweep output and the surface list it covered. (E02.02)

Continuity is a decision table with no blank cells. For each of missed payment, cancellation, lapse, later reactivation, venue sale, company acquisition, operator change, rebrand, merger, relocation, and an additional property brought by a new owner, the table states whether the EUR 1,000 rate survives, what happens to already-redeemed couple workspaces under the D-020 survival rule, and the notice period. Every finding disposed of in writing: fixed, or accepted by the founder with his stated reason. Nothing flagged and silently shipped.
No statutory reference, case citation or legal proposition appears in any published document unless verified against primary source text, with source and retrieval date in a citation register.

A written VAT and revenue-recognition position exists, sourced to current Revenue guidance, answering in order: accountable-person status by receipt of foreign B2B services, the tax point on annual prepayment, threshold aggregation, and OSS. The Revenue MyEnquiries reply is attached as evidence. Every agreement states the price as INCLUSIVE of VAT at the prevailing rate (D-021).

The contracting entity is correct and stated on every agreement (registered name and CRO number), or the founder has decided in writing to contract personally with the personal-liability exposure recorded as accepted.

GDPR operational paperwork current: Article 30 record, subprocessor register with each vendor DPA on file, documented transfer basis per non-EEA processor, and a written Article 35 DPIA threshold assessment reaching a reasoned conclusion either way.

An automated string check plus founder review confirms no published document, page, portal string, email, film line or proposal states or implies legal approval, solicitor review, accountant verification, or unqualified GDPR compliance. Pre-approved answers exist for the four questions venues ask.

The gate pass is recorded as founder-accepted without professional review, with the date and the founder own words. Never as legal review obtained or legally approved in any generated report.

releaseGates.name: Product
exitCriteria: The ratified couple access term is enforced by code end to end. studio/src/lib/entitlements-db/codes.ts accepts a computed duration and refuses anything shorter than 548 days rather than throwing on any value other than 548; the wedding date is stored on the sponsored entitlement at redemption; expiry is max(redemption + 548 days, wedding date + 90 days); and a wedding-date change recomputes expiry later, never earlier. Evidence: a named test covering all four behaviours plus the specific R-015 case, books March 2027, marries September 2028, redeems on signature. The gate fails while the mint guard is a hard equality on VENUE_EDITION_COUPLE_ACCESS_DAYS. (D-022, R-015, E04.07, E04.09, E04.12)

Unlimited entitlement is representable in all four places R-016 names: the mint path accepts an unlimited sponsor without the null-allotment throw; availableCount and the 'No remaining allotment headroom' attention item are suppressed for unlimited sponsors; the HQ near-allotment list excludes them; and studio/src/app/hq/entitlements/OnboardVenueForm.tsx no longer defaults the field to 10. Evidence: the four diffs plus a test asserting a portal payload for an unlimited sponsor contains no seat count, no remaining count and no headroom warning anywhere, including CSV export, PDF, tooltips, support view-as and accessibility text. (D-020, R-016, E07.03, E07.07, E07.08, E07.09)

Article 9 capture has a decided, implemented position. Either dietary and accessibility data is captured at a guest-facing RSVP step where the guest supplies their own data, or it stays couple-entered with all five R-017 controls shipped: structured fields not free text, hard exclusion from any public Timeline payload enforced by a test rather than a clause, retention tied to the wedding date, Article 9 named in the E03.01 role map with the condition relied on, and an under-16 rule. app/src/lib/templates.generated.ts and app/src/app/the-wedding/page.tsx both match the chosen position. Evidence: the code path, the exclusion test, the role-map entry, the two diffs. (R-017, E04.08, E05.03, E06.01)

The privacy boundary is a test, not a promise. One named test asserts that for a fully populated sponsored workspace the venue-visible payload contains no task title, note body, milestone story, photograph, collaborator name, guest name or free-text field, and that the same holds for the CSV export, the PDF report, the support view-as path and any email digest. Evidence: the test file and its output listing the surfaces covered. R-007 cannot be closed by copy review. (E04.08, E07.12, E07.18)

D-011's three ratified product rules are each enforced by a test: a wedding date appears in the portal only where that venue's code was redeemed; a wedding-date change never surfaces as a portal event; and suppression holds at 3 eligible sponsored workspaces for behavioural counts and 5 for percentage cohorts, with the suppressed number absent from tooltips, exports, view-as and accessibility text. Evidence: three named tests. (D-011, E04.09, E07.12)

Every lifecycle state in the E04.07 state machine has a deterministic fixture and a test, including unlink, couple separation, venue non-renewal with redeemed workspaces still live, release-on-cancellation with venue branding and name removed within 24 hours, postponement, expiry into Keepsake, and deletion. Evidence: the fixture manifest plus a test run showing one fixture per documented state with no state unrepresented. (E04.06, E04.07, E04.11, E04.12, D-020 points 2 and 3)

The Keepsake export exists as a produced artifact, not a plan. An export has been generated from a fixture workspace, opened by a human without Signal Studio present, and a test asserts it contains every published milestone plus every private item the couple owns. Evidence: the artifact's format and size, a screenshot of it open, and the test. D-010 point 3 makes the export the thing that keeps the Keepsake promise honest; a promise of an export is not an export. (E03.09, E06.11)

The three sharing modes survive adversarial test: a private link is unguessable with its entropy stated and revocation effective immediately; a password-protected artifact refuses without the password on every route including OG-image and metadata endpoints; and an unpublished artifact returns 404 from a previously cached link. Evidence: app/src/server/share-revocation-contract.test.mjs extended to the sponsored Timeline, named and passing. (E06.05, E06.12)

The design-system review is recorded as artifacts: pnpm ds:check clean in both app and studio, visual-regression baselines committed for every surface appearing in either film, and founder evidence captured at all four breakpoints through studio/scripts/experience/founder-evidence.mjs with its hashes intact. Evidence: the baseline directory, the check outputs, the evidence manifest. (E05.11, E05.12, E06.12, E07.18)

The audit D-015 Q2 mandated is legible. For each task in E04 through E07 the record states whether existing repository work fully satisfies, partially satisfies, or does not satisfy its written acceptance criteria, naming the file paths inspected. A-004 closes with a number rather than staying open. Evidence: the audit table, one row per task, with a total. (D-015 Q2, A-004)

The Account and the Portal are demonstrably one surface. A single authenticated session reaches invitation administration, adoption evidence, account standing, renewal date and support history without a second login or a second product; /hq/venue-portal-review still redirects to /hq/account-review; and no venue-facing string names two products. Evidence: ordered screenshots or a recording covering all five, plus the redirect test. (D-015 Q4, E07.01, E07.16)

End-to-end reconciliation passes on live data, not fixtures. For one venue account in the production-like environment, invitation count, redemption count, activation count and every figure in the generated PDF and CSV agree with the database, carry the same data-through date, and name the metric dictionary version. A single mismatch fails the gate rather than raising needs_attention. Evidence: the reconciliation run showing both sides. (E07.14, E07.15, E07.18, E09.09)

releaseGates.name: Data, security and reliability
exitCriteria: Cross-tenant isolation is proven by tests that try and fail. Named tests attempt to read and to write another venue's sponsors, codes, redemptions, rollups and reports, and to read a couple workspace from a venue session, each asserting refusal at the data layer rather than only at the route. Evidence: app/src/server/cross-tenant-isolation.test.mjs and tenant-scope.test.mjs extended with the sponsored-venue cases, named and passing. (E08.04, E08.05)

Every venue-facing and couple-facing route is enumerated in a committed manifest with its required role, and a test fails when a route exists without an entry. Anonymous, wrong-venue, wrong-role and revoked-member requests are each asserted refused. Evidence: app/scripts/check-route-manifest.mjs extended plus the authorisation-matrix test output. (E08.05, E07.18)

Invitation tokens survive five named attacks, one test each: guessing with entropy stated in bits and redemption rate-limited per address and per account with the enumeration arithmetic shown, reuse after redemption, forwarding to a different account, replay of a captured redemption request, and two concurrent redemptions of the same code. Evidence: five named tests, all passing. (E08.06)

A restore actually happened. pnpm recovery:drill is run against a real backup of every production database carrying venue or couple data; the restored copy is queried to confirm a known sponsored workspace and its redemptions are present; and wall-clock time from decision to restored is recorded. RPO and RTO are recorded as measured numbers, not targets. Evidence: the drill output with timestamps and the restored-row proof. A backup that has never been restored is not a backup. (E08.09)

The incident runbook names a person, a channel and a clock for each of: breach affecting couple data, breach affecting venue data, total outage, silent data corruption, and a wrongly issued or wrongly expired entitlement. It records the 72-hour GDPR Article 33 notification clock and where the DPC is contacted. It has been walked through once as a tabletop, and the absence of paid on-call is recorded as an accepted limitation of the zero budget. Evidence: the runbook and the tabletop record. (E08.08, E08.12, D-015 Q5)

Billing is tested with real money once, before any venue is invoiced. One founding agreement at EUR 1,000 is charged and refunded in production; the immutable founding-rate flag and historical price record are written and cannot be edited from the operator UI; the invoice states the price as inclusive of VAT at the prevailing rate; and the payment is individually identifiable so treatment can be corrected retrospectively. Evidence: the transaction ID, the refund ID, the invoice PDF showing the VAT wording, and the immutability test. (E08.01, E08.02, E15.02, D-021, R-018)

Renewal, failed payment, grace and lapse each fire against a clock in test: renewal invoice, reminder, failed-payment retry schedule, grace-period end, and lapse, with the D-020 survival rule asserted, that a lapsed venue's already-redeemed workspaces keep full term plus Keepsake and only new issuance stops. Evidence: a time-travel test covering all five transitions plus the survival assertion. (E08.03, D-020 point 2)

Upload handling is honest about what a zero budget buys: file type validated by content rather than extension, size limits enforced server-side, private storage with signed time-limited URLs, no user-supplied file served from an origin that can execute it, and EXIF stripped from milestone photographs. The absence of commercial malware scanning is recorded as an accepted residual with the founder's note. Evidence: the tests, the storage configuration, and the recorded residual. (E08.07)

Performance budgets are measured on the surfaces that carry the product's claim: the shared Timeline on a mid-range mobile over a throttled connection, the portal Overview, and the couple briefing. pnpm budgets:check and pnpm performance:measure produce recorded numbers against stated budgets and a regression fails the build. Evidence: the budget file, the measured run, the CI wiring. (E08.10)

Instrumentation reconciles across three layers at least once. A scripted run creates an invitation, redeems it, performs a first meaningful action, publishes a Timeline and enters Keepsake; each of those five transitions is asserted present in the event stream, in the daily rollup and in the venue's report, with counts matching at every layer, duplicate source events proven idempotent, and every number in the report carrying its metric dictionary version, denominator, reporting window and coverage state. Evidence: the script and its three-layer output. (E09.01, E09.02, E09.03, E09.09, E07.15)

The demonstration fixture is deterministic and its imagery's provenance is recorded. The one-action demo reset restores the canonical Glenmara House and Mara-and-Finn state identically across all four products and the portal on two consecutive runs; every demonstration image records how it was generated (model, prompt or source, date), because D-012 replaced licensing with generation and there is no licence to file; and a named reviewer confirms no unapproved real venue or couple material appears. Evidence: the reset diffed twice, the image provenance register, the reviewer verdict. (E09.06, E09.07, E09.08, E09.12, D-012, A-007, R-011)

Release engineering is executed, not documented. The three steps in studio/content/hq/operator-todos/open-signal-studio-2026-09-01.md are individually completed and ticked: the redeploy that flips the statically generated surfaces, the marketing-CTA decision, and the /app allowlist decision. Every venue-reachable URL is re-fetched after the deploy and confirmed to show post-launch state, and the rollback procedure has been executed once against a staging deploy. Evidence: the closed operator-todo, the post-deploy fetch of each URL, and the rollback run output. (E08.12, D-007, DEP-005)

releaseGates.name: Creative
exitCriteria: Every deliverable render has a manifest that validates against signal-motion/src/render/manifest-schema.ts, and each manifest's output.sha256 matches the file on disk when re-hashed by the Claude lane. Evidence: the manifest paths and the Claude-lane re-hash output. A render without a passing manifest is not a deliverable. (E13.17, E14.17)

No deliverable was rendered from a dirty tree. Every manifest records code.dirty false and a code.gitSha that resolves to a commit on a pushed branch. Evidence: git cat-file -e per manifest, run by the Claude lane. This is the single criterion that makes every other creative criterion reproducible. (E13.17, E14.18)

corepack pnpm verify passes in signal-motion at the exact commit the deliverables were rendered from: typecheck, tests, check:deps, check:ds, check:assets, check:copy-fit, check:compositions, check:motion, check:docs, and remotion compositions. Evidence: the full command output with the SHA, run by the Claude lane at that SHA rather than pasted from the motion lane.

A licence register in signal-motion/docs/ gives, per audio and font asset, the source URL, the licence name, the retrieval date, and the specific permission for commercial use in an email to businesses. Every distinct assets[].sha256 in the deliverable manifests appears in the register. The register must cover the music and sound bed even though scripts/write-render-manifest.mts currently populates assets[] from FONT_ASSETS only, so the manifests alone cannot close R-012. Evidence: the register, the hash cross-check, and the diff extending the manifest writer to audio. (E13.13, E14.16, R-012)

The Cohort 1 deliverables are 25 distinct files, each named to the project fixture composition profile convention, each with a distinct output.sha256, and each tied by manifest input.sha256 to the specific venue record it was rendered for. Evidence: 25 paths, 25 distinct hashes, and the venue-to-render mapping. Two identical hashes means two venues received the same film. (E13.15, E13.17)

Each of the 25 renders is checked frame-accurately for the two things that break a personalised film. The Claude lane extracts a still at the recipient-highlight frame for all 25, contact-sheets them, and records per render that the correct venue name is shown and that no other venue's name is legible, per the E13.05 anonymity rule and E10.14 consent status. Evidence: the contact sheet and a 25-row verdict list. (E13.05, E13.06, E13.17, E10.14)

Every word of on-screen and spoken copy in both films exists as text in the repository, and the same automated string check used by the legal gate runs over those files with zero hits for 'forever', 'for life', 'lifetime', 'guaranteed', 'GDPR compliant', 'legally approved', 'solicitor' or 'reviewed by'. Copy that exists only inside a composition's JSX cannot be checked and fails this criterion. Evidence: the copy files and the check output. (D-016, R-008, E13.07, E13.09, E14.12)

Before the Day contains no price. A stills sweep of the full master at a stated frame interval, plus the on-screen copy file, confirms no euro sign, no '1,500', no '1,000' and no price wording anywhere in the film. Evidence: the sweep output and the copy file. D-014 ratified this and the film is the easiest place to lose it. (D-014, E14.13)

Product-accuracy QA is a comparison, not an assertion. For every product surface appearing in Before the Day, a still from the film sits beside the frozen product screenshot from the E09.12 demo reset, and a named reviewer records whether the film shows a screen the product can actually produce. Any invented UI, invented metric or invented copy is listed explicitly. Evidence: the paired stills and a per-surface verdict. (E14.18, R-004, R-007)

Privacy QA is verdict-per-claim. Every frame or line in either film that states or implies what the venue does or does not see is listed, and each is matched to the shipped behaviour verified by the product gate's privacy test, by test name. A claim the product cannot demonstrate is cut, not softened. Evidence: the claim list with a test name against every row. (E14.12, E14.18, R-007)

Generated faces are handled per R-011. The record lists every shot containing a generated human face, and each is either absent from the deliverable or the founder has looked at that specific shot and accepted it in writing. Evidence: the shot list and the founder note. The mitigation was no close-up generated faces; the gate requires the list to exist so the mitigation can be seen to have held. (R-011, D-012, E14.06, E14.09)

The E13.08 price sequence is genuinely parameterised: the composition's props schema carries the two figures as data, so a commercial change is a re-render rather than an animation rebuild. Evidence: the props schema and one render at altered figures. This is A-002, which no gate previously checked. (A-002, E13.08)

Delivery is complete and re-openable by someone who is not the motion lane: 16:9 master, captions as a sidecar file, transcript, the 9:16 and 1:1 cutdowns, the archive structure, and the Cohort 2 to 4 rerender procedure. The Claude lane has followed that procedure once, unaided, to produce one throwaway render from scratch. Evidence: the file list and the output of the Claude-lane rerender with its manifest. A procedure nobody outside the authoring lane has executed is not a procedure. (E13.18, E14.17)

releaseGates.name: Sales readiness
exitCriteria: Cohort 1 is 25 named venues in the CRM, each carrying a verified buyer contact with a verification date within 30 days of the send, a verified email address, coordinates that plot inside the 45-minute drive-time ring, eligibility confirmed against D-012's in and out venue-type lists, and one written venue-specific reason it belongs. Evidence: the CRM completeness export by field, held in Signal HQ and never in the project tree. Any blank verification date means the cohort is not locked. (E10.06, E10.07, E10.08, E10.11, E10.12, R-005)

The researched universe is at least 125 accounts, or the shortfall is formally documented with the number actually found and what was searched. Deduplication is complete across venue groups, multi-property hotels, shared operators and renamed properties, with the number of merged rows recorded. Evidence: the universe count and the dedup log. This is the criterion that says out loud whether 25 signed venues is arithmetically available. (E10.04, E10.05)

Deliverability is proven before the first real send, not assumed. SPF, DKIM and DMARC pass on signalstudio.ie as shown by raw headers on a real received message rather than by a DNS record existing; the domain's sending history is stated; and an inbox-placement test to a seed set across Gmail, Outlook and one Irish ISP records where each message landed. Evidence: the raw headers, the seed results, the dates. (E11.04, R-010)

Sending mechanics match D-013 exactly and are verifiable from the sent message rather than the configuration screen: film link-click tracking on, open tracking off with no tracking pixel present in the HTML, a one-click unsubscribe header, and a suppression list honoured by the sending path. Evidence: the raw source of a real test send showing no pixel and the unsubscribe header, plus a test that a suppressed address is refused. (D-013 point 3, E11.04, E03.11)

The complete sequence has been rehearsed once, end to end, against a rehearsal account before any real venue is touched: introduction email sent and received, film link clicked, meeting booked through the booking flow, discovery structure used, walkthrough delivered, proposal and order form issued, 14-day hold started, and the account moved through every CRM stage including 'later' after the fourth touch. Evidence: the rehearsal account's full stage history, the artifacts produced at each step, and a written list of what broke. A sequence never walked is a document, not a system. (E11.02, E11.05, E11.08 to E11.11, E11.13, E11.14, D-013 point 4)

The venue marketing-controls package exists and is attached to the agreement, not only to the pack: the approved copy pack, a one-page prohibited-claims sheet naming 'forever', 'guaranteed', permanence or storage promises, 'GDPR compliant' and any claim that legal review was obtained, and the clause in the master agreement requiring correction within a stated period. Evidence: the copy pack, the sheet, and the clause reference in the E03.02 draft. R-020 is the only risk on the register that reaches outside Signal Studio's own strings. (R-020, E03.02, E12.12)

Every commercial surface a Cohort 1 venue can reach is enumerated as a list and QA'd per dimension: the public landing page, the private Founding 25 invitation page, the parameterised proposal page, the film landing destination, the certificate, the sales kit, the deck and the one-page proposal.
